files.text:
"""Shows the most recent `window` samples. The worker stays across runs
(reuseWorker); each run starts with an empty window."""
from collections import deque

from inputs.sample.live.Sample import Sample

points = None


def on_run_start(ctx):
    global points
    points = deque(maxlen=ctx.params().Window())


def main(ctx):
    s = ctx.input("sample", Sample)
    points.append((s.Index(), s.Value()))
    xs = [float(i) for i, _ in points]
    ys = [v for _, v in points]
    mean = sum(ys) / len(ys)
    ctx.display_line_chart([
        {"id": "value", "label": "random walk", "x": xs, "y": ys},
        {"id": "mean", "label": f"mean of last {len(ys)}", "x": [xs[0], xs[-1]], "y": [mean, mean]},
    ])

Sends the seed, the count, the interval and the first state.
Takes one step, sends the value to plot, and returns the next state to its own input. This loop of wires goes round until the set count.

intro: A demo that makes one value of a random walk every 100 ms and draws it as a line chart in real time.
finale: After the set number of values, no next state came out and the stream ended. In the app you can stop it partway, and the chart up to there stays.
